action_items.task: Research the feasibility of voice activation for the embedded system.
Look at the speaker and LED design for locating the remote.
Provide the frequency data for the most common options used by people.
Email the team if anything is missed or needs rectification.

decisions.text: Decided to use black and white displays to reduce unit costs.
Decided to target the general public who have used mobile phones.
Decided the remote will feature a joystick for channel and volume control, plus menu and okay buttons.
Decided to focus the remote on television control only, excluding interactive functions.
Incorporate a speaker and LED into the remote for locating it.
The double arc shape will be used for the enter button.

notes:
## Previous Meeting Minutes Review
- Introduced the possibility of a macro facility, interacting with the TV, bar-code, joystick for user manipulation, and ergonomics of the remote control.
- Teletext has become outdated due to the popularity of the internet.
- Remote control should only be used for the TV.
- Corporate image should stay recognisable, including colour and slogan.
## Voice Recognition Feasibility
- Voice recognition software exists already as open source.
- People are willing to pay extra for voice recognition software.
- Voice recognition works well for a fixed vocabulary (e.g., channel numbers) but may be impractical for frequent use like changing channels.
- Voice recognition requires microphones in the remote control, which is an unusual feature.
- Options include voice recognition alone (impractical for night time or visitors) or voice recognition combined with a regular remote.
- Removing the regular remote part allows the device to be designed freely (shape, size, fancy appearance).
- Concerns include training time, regional accents, and user returns due to speed compared to button presses.
## User Interface Design Approaches
- Two main trends exist: button-heavy interfaces (like early remotes) which are user-unfriendly, and user-focused designs that pare down to essential functions like channel and volume control.
- A preferred approach is a programmable design with a full range of functions accessible via a minimal number of controls, such as a joystick, allowing users to specify their most likely needs.
- Inspiration is drawn from game controllers like the PlayStation, using distinctive geometrical shapes for basic functions with further specification dependent on the mode.
## Hardware and Internal Design
- The Industrial Designer presented the internal layout of the remote, including the energy source, user interface, sender, chip, and digital signal transmission to the TV.
- Options discussed include using many buttons versus many light bulbs to indicate appliance status, and the feasibility of adding a joystick which would require more components.
- An alternative concept involves a small display (slightly larger than a mobile phone) to traverse menus and control functionality, alongside common buttons for volume and channel changes.
## Display and Cost
- Agreed to use black and white displays to keep unit costs down, with color as a potential future development.
## Target Audience
- Decided to target most people who have used a mobile phone, relying on their existing experience.
## Remote Features and Design
- The remote will include a small joystick for channel changes, volume control, and menu navigation, alongside standard up/down buttons.
- Decided to include two function buttons: a menu button and an 'okay' button to prevent joystick misinterpretation.
- Design constraint: The remote must be controllable one-handedly with the joystick operated by the thumb.
## Locating the Remote Control
- Consider adding a speaker and LED to the remote for locating it via sound and light.
- The LED can be incorporated into the base of the TV unit to flash when the remote is found.
- Small key-rings have both sound and light, suggesting this is a viable design touch.
## Transmitter and Power Source
- The transmitter could be built into the television itself if targeting TV manufacturers.
- The electronics can be placed externally or internally without affecting the final product.
- This approach could open up a new potential market.
## Slogan and Branding
- The slogan 'Fashion in Electronics' was proposed to be printed on the plastic.
- The 'two Rs' logo was suggested as an alternative to 'Real Reaction'.
## Button Design
- The double arc shape on the remote could serve as the enter button.
tldr: The team finalized the design of a new remote control focusing on television control with a joystick, black and white display, and locating features, while dropping teletext and voice recognition.
